# `kernel/attestation/DescriptorHashStore.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/attestation/DescriptorHashStore.js`

DescriptorHashStore.js — persists approved tool/resource/prompt descriptor hashes IDB-side, so a "rug pull" (descriptor silently changing after the user approved it) is detected across sessions, not just within one runtime (that in-memory check is webgpu-os/kernel/tools/MetadataRugPullDetector.js). Hashing reuses the same SHA-256 primitive as packages/PackageVerifier.js (contentHashHex from engine/core/math/ChecksumMath.js) rather than a new hashing routine. Storage reuses the generic 'kv' IndexedDB store (see storage/IndexedDBDriver.js) instead of adding a new object store/migration.

| `hashPortableDescriptor` | `static async hashPortableDescriptor(descriptor)` | Stable signed-contract hash used by Faculty manifests. Release builds may minify function spelling, so this projection uses the declared, package-signed implementationHash when one is present. It must never be used for live approval or rug-pull checks; hashDescriptor() binds the exact callable code for those decisions. |
| `getApprovedRecord` | `async getApprovedRecord(name)` |  |
| `signedBuiltInWitness` | `async signedBuiltInWitness(name, descriptor, { facultyId = null, publisherId = null, } = {})` | Return a content-free proof only when the current callable is the exact live emission approved by one signed built-in Faculty revision. This is stricter than a normal operator descriptor approval and is intended for mutation lanes whose planner surface must not accept injected lookalikes. |
| `approve` | `async approve(name, hash)` |  |
| `approveSignedBuiltInRevision` | `async approveSignedBuiltInRevision(name, descriptor, proof)` | Atomically bind a live descriptor to a package-policy-verified ring-0 Faculty revision. The exact handler/verifier text is a per-runtime tamper canary. Durable authority comes from the package-signed portable descriptor, which deliberately survives raw/minified emission changes. A clean runtime may therefore rebind a verified emission, while an exact callback change observed by this store instance is always rejected. |

## Functions

### `descriptorMeaningSnapshot(descriptor)`

Complete approval identity for a callable descriptor. This intentionally includes authority, mutability, effect, provenance, timeout, and executable source fields so retaining the same JSON input schema cannot conceal a more dangerous implementation after approval.

### `portableDescriptorMeaningSnapshot(descriptor)`

Package-portable descriptor identity for signed Faculty manifests only.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
